name: The Ascendant
description:
Words set down by an unnamed chronicler:

"Their arrival in this world was marked by a great crashing, as of a rending of the sky. This came in the middle of the night, and we found ourselves all thrust awake together, blood surging, feeling the world reverberating with a great sound but without having heard the sound itself. Looking upward, we saw a blue, whirling vortex tearing across the sky like a violent, twisting vein of stars. Thousands of wisps of light descended from it and settled amid the folds of the earth.

In fear we watched as these wisps - these beings - moved slowly over the land, aimless at first. We followed them, watching their strange, hovering movement in awe. They are like we are when we dream of flying - a pure essence of being, untethered and uninhibited.

In the days that followed we found that they seemed to be gathering in old places: ruins, temples, shrines - places of great fear and wonder. For a time they hovered there in some state of contemplation, their thoughts made manifest within their swirling forms as visions of we knew not what: Their own memories? Events of this world past and future?

Though they took no notice of us or of the offerings we left for them, we came to believe that they had been sent here to bring gifts to us - or rather to unlock gifts hidden within our own world. Indeed I saw with my own eyes how they drew something luminous and blue out of old stones, ancient groves and deep pools. This power, this light, they took within themselves, but so great was its quantity that part of it was also scattered through the air in all directions. Those of us who dared to touch it found that we could wield it.

And so it was that these beings - who we came to call The Ascendant - gave to this world what we now call magic.

There was a time of great joy among us as we played with this new magic together, discovering the contours of its power. And for a time we left the Ascendant unregarded as they continued their harvest - for a harvest it was, as we soon learned. The places they had visited began to die: the fear, the wonder, the color draining right out of them, a blight spreading outward like a grey stain upon the land.

Some of us turned to anger, feeling our joy turn sour as we realized its cost. Even with our newfound powers, our attacks against The Ascendant were as pebbles against a rampart - or rather as pebbles through thin air, since they continued to take absolutely no notice of us.

One day we awoke feeling anticipation permeating the air, and news came from near and far that The Ascendant were gathering in the place where they had first appeared. Stranger still, it was rumored that some of the Ascendant were lingering and had begun communicating with mortal folk with great urgency. It seems there was dissent among them and these few wanted to enlist our help in some way, wanted to stay in this world with the magic they had taken from it.

Before we could learn the full truth of this, the great event occurred a second time. The sky was opened, the twisting vein of stars appeared and The Ascendant rose to meet it. With a great crash that broke the earth, they were gone, leaving behind the gaping silence of our scarred world. We stood bereft of will, our anger impotent and the magic in our hands a symbol of our soiled joy."

This tale of the arrival and departure of The Ascendant has passed from legend to myth to nursery rhyme, but there are those who maintain that some few of them did indeed stay, and that they walk among us...

⁂ ⁂ ⁂

PART OF HISTORY

If you use this world module, the above account is more or less true: The Ascendant came here, extracted magic from this world, and left (mostly), granting the peoples of the world the "gift" of magic in the process. This may be woven into the history of your campaign world however you choose. Questions to consider while so weaving:

  • How long ago were The Ascendant here? How long did they stay?

  • Where did they congregate and how did their work change those places?

  • What was the state of the world at the time of these events? How was it disrupted?

  • What were the effects of magic being suddenly loosed upon the world? Who used it for good? Who used it for ill? Who rose to power and who fell?

  • To what degree do these events continue to shape the world today? Are The Ascendant generally revered, feared, reviled, forgotten, or a mixture of all?

THE ASCENDANT AMONG US

However you choose to answer these questions, one thing that is for certain is that some small number of the Ascendant did indeed stay behind, somehow tethering themselves to this world. That tethering was also a severing - breaking their connection to whatever force brought them here, cutting them off from their memories, and suppressing their Ascendant state, though a great power remains within them.

These people - these Ascendant walking among us - can play whatever role you choose in your story. Some may be troubled and are wielding their latent power recklessly as villains. Some may be strange wanderers who perform impossible feats for the benefit of others. Some may find relief by meting out their power into works that they put into the world.

And some of them may be you:

ASCENDANT PLAYER CHARACTERS

When using this world module, every player character has a chance of having a hidden Ascendant origin, which is hidden from both them and from the player that pilots them:

PREVALENCE IN THE WORLD

First, choose a die type to determine how prevalent this Ascendant origin should be among the heroes you create. Choose a d2 if you want it to be a big part of your story, choose a d20 if you want it to be a rare and unexpected element, or choose somewhere in between (d4, d6, d8, d10, d12) as appropriate. The group should come to consensus on this choice.

CHARACTER CREATION

Whenever one of you creates a new player character, another player rolls a die of the chosen type in secret. On a 1, the character is one of the Ascendant who stayed behind, though they do not know it. The player who performed the roll is the keeper of that information, and they are responsible for sharing that information with each GM who runs a Quest that includes the character. The player who created the Ascendant character should remain unaware of all this.

HINTS AND THE GM ROLE

During each Quest, the GM is responsible for weaving hints at the character's Ascendant origins into the story in subtle ways: through interactions with the environment and NPCs, as part of Soft and Hard Moves they take, as part of the outcomes of BANE and BOON, and particularly if the character experiences a Bout of Madness.

The manner in which you give these hints as GM is up to you. Perhaps they experience brief visions that are memories from their severed, Ascendant past. Perhaps they have some unusual physical characteristic that expresses itself to a different degree at different times. Perhaps actions they take will occasionally have a much greater effect than expected. Perhaps they feel a pull or aversion to the sites where the Ascendant (possibly they themselves) performed their work. Perhaps they feel a pull or aversion to NPCs or other PCs who share this heritage.

Whatever you choose, it is the task of the GM to weave these hints into the game in a way that is subtle enough to allow the player to discover the character's true nature slowly over time. The pace of that discovery is up to you, but they should eventually discover it, as determined by the following:

DISCOVERING ASCENDANT ORIGINS

The character may discover their Ascendant origin by rolling Spirit against a Difficulty. That Difficulty starts at 32 when the character is created. Each time a GM introduces a hint at the character's Ascendant origin into the game, reduce the Difficulty by 2 - regardless of whether the player or their character notices the significance of it. This Difficulty is part of the information kept by the player who also holds the knowledge of the character's Ascendant origin.

A roll to attempt to discover Ascendant origin should only ever be initiated by a player. Any player may spend an action to make such a roll at any time. A character who is not of Ascendant origin always fails the roll, but may make the roll as many times as they like. When a roll is made:

  • On a pass, the character discovers their Ascendant origin. They gain and immediately activate the Go Ascendant ability.

  • On a failure, the character learns nothing and checks a Condition.

Note that making such a roll does not affect the Difficulty - it remains the same.

THE ASCENDANT AND INTERMEZZO

Visits to the sites where the Ascendant performed their work may be incorporated into Quests, but the following Intermezzo activity is also available to all player characters:

VISIT A SITE OF THE ASCENDANT: You travel to visit one of the sites where the Ascendant extracted magic from the earth. The Intermezzo must be long enough to accommodate the travel involved and at least one day spent at the site. When a player chooses this activity for their character, all other players must confer in secret:

  • If the character is of Ascendant origin, this group is responsible for agreeing on a hint to deliver to the player, acting collectively as GM to weave the hint into the experience the character has at the site.

  • If the character is not of Ascendant origin, this group is responsible for agreeing on some information about the world related to the Ascendant, the site, its environs or people connected to it, acting collectively as GM to weave the information into the experience the character has at the site.

Either way, the character may choose to make one roll during this Intermezzo activity to attempt to discover their Ascendant origin, as described above. Also either way, the group should consider the significance of the place and the visit for the character, awarding Shadow if it's a negative experience and awarding Hope or removing Shadow if it's a positive experience.

FURTHER QUESTIONS TO CONSIDER

As you navigate all this consider these questions:

  • What is the ultimate origin of The Ascendant? Were they once mortal beings tethered to one world or were they brought into being as a wandering cosmic force?

  • What set The Ascendant in motion? What propels them now? What do they gain by extracting the magic from worlds? What ultimate goal are they pursuing?

  • Why did some of The Ascendant choose to stay behind in this world? What was the act that allowed them to do so? What was the role of the folk of this world from whom they required help?

  • Did The Ascendant who stayed behind transform into mortal form or do they inhabit the bodies of others? If the former, how they make sense of their long life? If the latter, do they lengthen the life of their host or do they jump from body to body as each expires (and what, if anything, do they remember about these lives they've lived)?

  • To what degree does their power derive from the magic they harvested from this world? If they took it, can they give it back? Can it be taken back from them?

These questions can be explored and answered by GMs as they choose, or can be included in the list of campaign questions (see the Campaign Creation section of the rules).
